newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices seen firming on export hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices seen firming on export hopes.

text.p: Cotton prices are expected rise in the near term on speculative buying in Indian markets on hopes the government might allow further exports, dealers said on Thursday.

"Cotton buying from textile and yarn mills has been low. But speculators have turned active," said a trader. "At the same time, crop arrivals from the 1996/97 season (Oct/Sept) have also slackened to some extent."
The government has so far authorised export of 1.22 million 170-kg bales in 1996/97.
Traders said the total quantity earmarked for export in the current season had risen to 1.65 million bales, including a surplus of 430,000 bales from the previous season.
Traders said they were hopeful the government would allow another 200,000 bales for export following a fresh assessment of the 1996/97 crop by the official Cotton Advisory Board (CAB).
The CAB, which met last week in Bombay, had estimated the 1996/97 crop at 16 million bales, the same as in the previous season.
CAB chairman B.C. Khatua said the agency was concerned about falling cotton prices, fuelling hopes about the government authorising further exports to lift the subdued domestic market.

The federal budget for 1997/98 (April/March), presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram last week, reduced import duty on synthetic yarn which, analysts said, would affect cotton consumption to some extent.
The budget proposed to reduce excise duty on polyester fibre yarn (PFY) by 11.5 percent to 34.5 percent and polyester staple fibre (PSF) by 2.3 percent to 20.7 percent.
"More synthetic yarn will be blended with cotton by mills, thereby affecting cotton consumption," said a trader.
Another budgetary proposal that helped cotton prices firm has been the government's decision to allow resumption of futures trading in cotton.
In the week to Thursday, Bengal-deshi gained 50/60 rupees to 840/890 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and Punjab saw-ginned rose 25/45 rupees to 1,460/1,665. F-414 gained 15/20 to 1,850/1,870.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) rose 100 to 11,500/11,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
